messages:
alex_m: Heads-up — state migration for eu-region hit a parity gap during the rollout. I kicked a move across accounts and now downstream reconciles are failing with leftover lease entries.
jia: Ack. CI canary failed for the gpu-workspaces. It looks like the gitops import ran while the migration script was still writing the new state files.
sam_k: Can you paste the apply error? I saw something similar last quarter but that was a TTL mismatch.
alex_m: Apply output snippet:```
Error: Error locking state: dynamodb: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
  on main.tf line 12, in resource "aws_dynamodb_table_item":
  12: resource "aws_dynamodb_table_item" "lock" { ... }
```
alex_m: But when I inspected the lock table the item has a TTL that's set to 0 (never expires) and the LockID prefix doesn't match the new workspace key. Looks like migration wrote the blob with old prefix.
infra-bot: Automated note: migration-job-37 exited with status=0 at 2025-11-02T14:02Z; copy step retried 3x.
jia: Root cause hypothesis: two writers — the legacy migration script and the gitops import — used different key namespaces (s3 prefix changed from "workspaces/" to "ws/"), so the dynamo lock for the new key wasn't created, but the old lock entry stayed behind and is conflicting because terraform checks both naming variants in our custom lock resolver.
sam_k: Ugh. That explains the TTL=0. The migration tool didn't set ttl_attr due to an edgecase when it bumped the key version.
alex_m: Short plan: 1) delete the stale lock items for affected workspaces 2) re-run the import/apply with strict -lock-timeout and backoff 3) add a preflight in gitops to wait for no active locks.
jia: For the delete step I'll run this (dry-run first):
```bash
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name infra-state-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "workspace/eu-gpu-42"}}'
aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name infra-state-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "workspace/eu-gpu-42"}}'
```
sam_k: Please don't use -lock=false in the apply. Manual deletion + a reconciliation gate is safer. We should also add retries in the CI job: attempt apply up to 4 times with exponential backoff and a 30s jitter.
alex_m: I'll patch the migration tool to set TTL and preserve the LockID namespace mapping. Will also add an idempotency check so it doesn't write duplicate keys.
infra-bot: Note: created ticket INFRA-2219 for migration changes, linked to INC-3456.
jia: Ops change for gitops pipeline: insert step `check-state-lock` that runs a small script to poll dynamo until there are no active locks for the target prefix (timeout 10m). If locks persist, fail the reconcile and notify oncall.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-3456 created and assigned to alex_m. Pager duty page-up in 5.
sam_k: After cleanup we should also run a small test: create a temporary workspace, import, and do an apply in the eu region under simulated concurrent gitops to verify no race.
alex_m: Agreed. I'll do cleanup now and post results. If anyone else sees other affected workspaces ping me :party_parrot:
